hints: Look closely at the number of hydrogen atoms in each formula, they all have C18 and O2, so the H number is your clue.
Remember saturated means no C=C double bonds, so it holds the maximum H atoms, and every C=C you add removes 2 H atoms.
walkthrough:
**Recall what saturated means**

Think of saturated as fully loaded with hydrogen. There are no carbon-carbon double bonds in the hydrocarbon chain, only single bonds.

That means a saturated fatty acid will have more H atoms than any unsaturated one with the same number of carbons.

**Use the general rule for fatty acids**

A saturated fatty acid with n carbons follows:
$$C_n H_{2n} O_2$$
So for $n = 18$:
$$H = 2 \times 18 = 36$$
Giving $C_{18}H_{36}O_2$.

**Pick the maximum H**

Option A has 36 H, the maximum. Options B, C and D have fewer H atoms, so each missing pair of 2 H tells you a double bond has replaced single bonds. That makes them unsaturated.

options.A: Correct, $C_{18}H_{36}O_2$ fits $C_nH_{2n}O_2$ with maximum H, so no double bonds and fully saturated.
options.B: Has 2 fewer H than saturated, so it has one C=C double bond and is monounsaturated.
options.C: Has 4 fewer H than saturated, so it has two C=C double bonds and is polyunsaturated.
options.D: Has 6 fewer H than saturated, so it has three C=C double bonds and is polyunsaturated.
